title: Caerlum Rising
premise: Dominic Okafor has survived the Thornfell mountains by being nobody: a smuggler who speaks to beasts in secret, since beast-speaking was outlawed when the crown began binding animals into war-engines. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes from the sky on the same night, Dominic is dragged into a rebellion led by Serah Vane, a disgraced ward-keeper, and a ragtag found family of outcasts. They discover the 'usurper' is no man at all but an ancient hunger wearing King Aldric's body, and that only a beast-speaker can reach what remains of the king inside it. Dominic must choose between staying hidden and safe or unbinding Aldric at the cost of revealing their gift—and their heart—to Serah. In the end, Dominic frees the king by offering the thing wearing his crown their own voice as bait, shattering its hold at the price of nearly losing theirs, and the restored king abolishes the binding laws as the stars return.
about_author: Odile Oyelaran is a former wildlife rehabilitator who grew up in three countries and writes fantasy about creatures that talk back. She lives near a forest she insists listens to her.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine run through Thornfell with a mule named Bramble establishes Dominic's hidden gift, their careful invisibility, and the mountain roads they know better than anyone. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. The border wards fail and the sky goes black; Serah, exiled for warning of exactly this, watches soldiers march under a lightless heaven. Emotional beat: vindication curdled into dread.

chapters.title: What Bramble Refused
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Bramble panics before dawn—beasts feel the wards dying—and Dominic shelters a wounded stranger who turns out to be Serah, fleeing crown riders. Emotional beat: instinct versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Secrets
chapters.summary: Dual-tension chapter, mostly Serah's POV. Serah deduces Dominic's gift from how the wild things behave; instead of reporting them, she asks for help crossing Thornfell to the free cities. Emotional beat: wary bargain struck between two people with everything to lose.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV, brief and fractured. Inside the palace, something ancient wears his body like a glove while his true mind screams beneath. Emotional beat: horror and fading hope.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Guiding Serah south, they gather unlikely companions: Tamsin, a deserter cook; Old Wren, a blind cartographer; and Kess, a child who talks to crows too openly. Emotional beat: the first fragile stitches of found family.

chapters.title: The Binding Yards
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The party witnesses a crown convoy hauling chained, bound beasts toward the front—war-engines made of enslaved minds. Dominic nearly breaks cover to free one. Emotional beat: rage against the law that criminalizes compassion.

chapters.title: Crows Bring Bad News
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Her crows report the usurper's armies moving faster than any human army could; the thing in the crown is feeding on the land itself. Emotional beat: childhood innocence cracking against war.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Disagree
chapters.summary: Old Wren's POV. Arriving at Merrowgate, the party finds the free cities' council squabbling, unwilling to believe the king is gone. Emotional beat: frustration—the enemy isn't just the usurper but denial.

chapters.title: An Audience of Cowards
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah pleads the case before the council; a crown envoy arrives and accuses her of treason, forcing the party to flee the city as wanted fugitives. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institutions meant to protect.

chapters.title: Underground, Under Stars
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hiding in caverns where no starlight reaches, Dominic realizes the vanished stars aren't destroyed—they're being eaten, and the caves still hum with old ward-magic Serah once kept. Emotional beat: hope rekindled in darkness.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Table
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In hiding, Tamsin cooks a real meal for the group, and the found family solidifies around shared stories and grief. Emotional beat: warmth as rebellion—choosing each other.

chapters.title: The Price of the Gift
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Serah asks Dominic directly to use beast-speaking to scout the army; Dominic confesses why they hide it—a sibling executed for the same gift. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the deepest trust.

chapters.title: Scouting the Hungry Host
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Speaking through wolves and ravens, Dominic sees the truth: the usurper's soldiers are half-bound themselves, puppets strung on stolen starlight. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Map
chapters.summary: Old Wren's POV. Wren reveals the palace sits atop the first binding-stone, the source of the crown's power, and draws a route in from memory before quietly arranging to stay behind as decoy. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Decoy at Dusk
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Wren's diversion works, but he is captured; the family escapes toward the capital carrying his map and his grief. Emotional beat: loss teaching the cost of the cause.

chapters.title: Into the Crown City
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Using smuggler routes and crow-scouts, the party infiltrates the capital as the bound-army musters outside its walls. Emotional beat: dread and determination walking hand in hand.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the throne room, Dominic meets the usurper face to face and hears, beneath its voice, Aldric's mind crying out. It offers Dominic safety and legitimacy if they kneel. Emotional beat: temptation measured against love and duty.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax part one. With Serah holding the failing wards open and Kess's crows disrupting the guards, Dominic reaches into Aldric's mind—but the hunger turns on Dominic's own voice, trying to devour their gift. Emotional beat: the fight for the self.

chapters.title: Bait of My Own Voice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax part two. Dominic offers their beast-speech as bait, luring the hunger out of Aldric's body, and Serah seals it in the collapsing binding-stone. Dominic loses their gift—at least seemingly—as the stars begin to return. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved by refusing to choose between them.

chapters.title: The King Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Freed and hollowed by guilt, Aldric publicly abolishes the binding laws and names the smugglers, deserters, and children who saved him. Wren is freed in the aftermath. Emotional beat: restoration earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Caerlum Rising
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. On a Thornfell ridge under returned stars, Dominic whispers to Bramble—and Bramble answers, the gift not lost but changed. Surrounded by their chosen family, Dominic finally stops hiding. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, in the open air.
